title: Private/VPC: maintenance window, offline upgrade packaging, and air-gapped deployment requirements
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Define concrete requirements and acceptance criteria for performing scheduled maintenance and upgrades of Redwood Private deployments in VPC and fully air-gapped environments. Focus on allowed network flows, offline upgrade artifact distribution, maintenance window semantics, rollback behavior, and testable acceptance scenarios.
background: Customers running Redwood Private often operate in environments with strict egress restrictions or completely air-gapped clusters. Current upgrade docs assume availability of a customer registry or transient egress for pull; we need a vetted approach and acceptance criteria for: (1) online upgrades with constrained egress via allowed hosts/proxies, (2) fully offline upgrades using signed artifact bundles, and (3) clear maintenance window semantics to meet SLOs for sensitive customers.
scope_in: Requirements and acceptance criteria for upgrade packaging, delivery, pre-checks, maintenance window controls, network allowlist, rollback triggers, and operator runbooks for Private/VPC and air-gapped installs. Test definitions and minimal automation scripts to validate acceptance.
scope_out: Changes to runtime internals (kernel-level optimizations), Dedicated/GPU autoscaling policies, and hosted API upgrade procedures. This ticket does not implement CI/CD automation for on-prem customers—only defines requirements and acceptance tests and produces lightweight validation tooling.
requirements: Network: Define minimal egress endpoints and ports required for an 'online permitted' upgrade path (registry endpoints, time servers, telemetry endpoints). Provide explicit IP/domain allowlist and TLS requirements.

Air-gap packaging: Produce a signed offline upgrade bundle format (tar.gz or OCI archive) that includes all container images, Helm charts, CRD manifests, and a signed release manifest with checksums and GPG signature instructions.
Delivery: Document supported delivery mechanisms: customer-hosted registry import, archive transfer via SFTP/USB, and a verified import tool (local CLI) with checksum+signature verification.

Maintenance window semantics: Provide a scheduling API/CLI flag and operator checklist to declare maintenance windows; define expected downtime or degraded-service window and required customer notification messages.

Pre-upgrade checks: Automated validation script that verifies cluster prerequisites (Kubernetes version compatibility, node resource headroom, existing CR versions), and a blocking pre-check exit codeset.

Rollback: Define automatic rollback triggers (failed healthchecks, >X% error rate for Y minutes) and a manual rollback procedure using the same offline bundle format. Ensure stateful metadata consistency (KV migrations must be reversible or versioned).
Observability: Upgrade run must emit structured events to local logs and optionally to customer telemetry endpoints; include an 'upgrade-report' artifact with pre/post checksums and timing metrics.

Security: All bundles and registries must be signed; provide guidance for KMS integration for private keys and ephemeral credentials for import tooling. Include revocation guidance if a bundle is compromised.
Compatibility matrix: Document supported K8s versions and recommended resource reservations per node group for the upgrade path.

Acceptance automation: Define a small test harness operators can run post-upgrade: smoke endpoints, KV-read/write consistency, model-serving sanity check (sample inference), and latency/throughput quick check under synthetic load.
Documentation: Update Private install and upgrade runbooks with step-by-step air-gap import examples, checklist, and troubleshooting section.
Operator ergonomics: Provide CLI flags and a non-interactive mode for scripted upgrades catering to automation pipelines used by SRE teams.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: For an online-permitted VPC customer, a scripted upgrade completing from version A to B succeeds when only allow-listed domains/ips (provided in docs) are reachable. The validation harness returns exit code 0 and produces an upgrade-report artifact.

AC-2: For an air-gapped environment, an operator can import a signed offline bundle using the local import CLI without any outbound network connectivity. Bundle signature and checksums are verified during import; post-upgrade smoke tests pass.

AC-3: Maintenance window can be scheduled via CLI/manifest; upgrade respects the window boundaries. If upgrade exceeds the scheduled window by more than 'grace period' (configurable, default 30 minutes), the system auto-enters a safe-fail state and notifies operator via logs and upgrade-report.

AC-4: Rollback can be initiated automatically on configurable healthcheck failures: if healthchecks fail continuously for 5 minutes or error rate > 10% for 3 minutes, the system reverts to prior release and verifies KV consistency using versioned backups. Rollback report is generated.
AC-5: All artifacts in the offline bundle are signed; the import tool rejects bundles with invalid signatures. Test scenarios must include signature tampering and missing artifact cases.

AC-6: Post-upgrade functional tests (smoke + sample inference) succeed within defined SLAs: 99% of sample inference responses within 2x baseline latency and no more than 0.1% error rate across 1000 sample requests.

AC-7: Documentation and runbook pages updated and validated by Solutions Engineering through a checklist: one walkthrough of online upgrade and one walkthrough of air-gapped upgrade, each executed by a reviewer different from the implementer.
AC-8: Security review sign-off recorded (security_review_required=true) and KMS guidance included for at-rest private key handling in docs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Draft bundle spec and import CLI prototype; get initial feedback from two pilot customers (VPC with limited egress, fully air-gapped). Phase 2: Iterate on tooling and docs; add pre-checks and rollback automation. Phase 3: Formal acceptance tests with Solutions Engineering and Security; publish runbooks and sample bundles. Rollout gated on AC-1..AC-8 completion.
test_plan: T1: Network-restricted upgrade test — simulate allowlist-only egress and run online upgrade script; verify upgrade-report and smoke tests.
T2: Air-gap import test — provision a cluster with no egress, import signed bundle, run pre/post checks, and execute sample inference test suite.
T3: Failure injection — corrupt one image in bundle and verify import fails with descriptive error; replay with signature tamper and missing manifest.
T4: Rollback validation — force healthcheck failures post-upgrade and confirm automated rollback triggers and data integrity checks.
T5: Long-running window test — schedule very short maintenance window to validate safe-fail path when upgrade exceeds window.
notes: Coordinate with ENG runtime and infra teams for image signing and import tooling. Solutions Engineering to recruit two pilot customers (one highly restricted VPC, one fully air-gapped) for acceptance testing. Keep release artifacts small by stripping debug layers from images. Consider future follow-up work to integrate with customer's internal registries and SSO-based import authorization.
